name: Radio
description: Puts a sound through a night-time radio link: narrow and thin, fading in and out, with static that swells whenever the signal sinks, whistles off the station and voices pitched wrong on sideband.

params.name: Band
params.description: Which kind of reception. Medium wave is the fuller local station that fades slowly. Shortwave is narrower and fades faster and deeper, with the tone hollowing as it goes. Sideband has no carrier: Tuning moves every pitch, and the noise rushes up in the gaps.

params.name: Tuning
params.description: The dial. In the middle the station is tuned in. On Medium wave and Shortwave, moving off brings a whistle that rises with the distance while the sound thins and breaks up. On Sideband it shifts every pitch up or down by the same amount, so harmonies turn sour.

params.name: Drift
params.description: How much the dial wanders by itself. Low settings keep the station steady; high settings let it slide off and back, so whistles and pitch come and go.

params.name: Fading
params.description: How unsteady the path through the air is. The signal sinks and returns over seconds, and a hollow, phasing notch sweeps through the tone as it goes. At its lowest the signal is steady.

params.name: Static
params.description: Atmospheric noise: hiss, crackle and the crashes of distant storms. It is heard most when the signal fades, because the receiver turns itself up to follow the station.

params.name: Interference
params.description: How often other things share the frequency: a passing whistle, a burst of warbling data tones, a mains buzz, the garble of a neighbouring station. They come and go; more makes them more frequent and louder.

params.name: Bandwidth
params.description: How wide the receiver's filter is. Narrow is thin and nasal with less noise; wide lets through more bass, more treble and more hiss.

params.name: Speaker
params.description: The size of the loudspeaker. At its lowest it is a clean line output; turning it up shrinks it to a small boxy speaker with a honk in the middle that rasps when pushed.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the radio.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Models a radio link in outline, as the complex envelope around the station's carrier: an AM or upper-sideband transmitter, a two-path sky wave (a flat fade plus a late path with a turning carrier phase, after the approach of Watterson, Juroshek and Bensema, 'Experimental Confirmation of an HF Ionospheric Channel Model', with seeded smooth movements), static and neighbours added at the aerial, tuning, an IF filter, a detector, a square-root automatic gain and a small loudspeaker. Levels and rates were set by measurement, not taken from a source. Static, neighbours and the whistle follow how loud the part is (over about a second, within -24 to +9 dB of the -15 dBFS RMS level they were tuned at). Static holds for 14 s after the input stops, then fades over 4 s to exact silence. Output is mono.
